newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-JUVENTUS, REAL MADRID AND LIVERPOOL LEAD THE WAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS, REAL MADRID AND LIVERPOOL LEAD THE WAY.

text.p: Italy's Juventus, Spain's Real Madrid and England's Liverpool all won at the weekend to stay top in their domestic leagues.
ITALY - Juventus strengthened their grip on the title race with a clinical 2-0 victory over Lazio at the Olympic stadium on Sunday which opened up a four-point gap at the top of Serie A.
The European champions had two goals disallowed for offside but still won comprehensively with strikes in each half from Michele Padovano.
Juventus, with 33 points from 17 matches, have already secured the "Winter Championship" -- the accolade traditionally awarded to the team leading Serie A at its halfway stage.

Neither second-placed Sampdoria, who needed a controversial last- minute goal to earn a point at Fiorentina, nor Inter, beaten in a home match with Bologna for the first time in 20 years, look capable of keeping pace with the league leaders.
SPAIN - A hat-trick of headers by midfielder Luis Enrique Martinez saved manager Bobby Robson on Sunday as Barcelona came back from 2-0 down to win 4-2 in a sensational game at Real Betis.
With memories of a shock defeat by Hercules still fresh, the former England coach's job was undoubtedly on the line. But the victory left Barcelona within three points of leaders Real Madrid.

The result followed Real's own extraordinary 4-1 win at neighbours Atletico on Saturday. Raul Gonzalez scored twice and Dutchman Clarence Seedorf and Victor Sanchez one each for Real after Kiko Narvaez had put defending champions Atletico ahead.

ENGLAND - An afternoon which seemed about to give Kenny Dalglish a dream start as Newcastle manager ended in stunning anti-climax for the United faithful on Saturday when Southampton scored twice in the last two minutes to force a 2-2 home draw.

Newcastle, who appointed Dalglish as manager on Tuesday following Kevin Keegan's departure the previous week, were 2-0 up with only eight minutes to go thanks to goals from Les Ferdinand and Lee Clark.

But, with 88 minutes on the clock, Newcastle keeper Shaka Hislop dropped a cross allowing Neil Maddison to shoot home from close range and then, deep into injury time, Matt Le Tissier powered in a 25-metre drive.
Liverpool stayed top with a 3-0 win over Aston Villa, two points ahead of defending champions Manchester United, who stretched their unbeaten league run to 11 matches with a 2-0 win at Coventry.
Dutch striker Dennis Bergkamp inspired Arsenal to a 3-1 win over Everton on Sunday. They are third, a point behind Manchester United. Newcastle are fourth.
FRANCE - Paris St Germain, humiliated by Juventus in the European Super Cup, recovered some of their badly dented pride with a 3-0 French Cup first round win at third division Besancon on Sunday.
PSG went ahead in the eighth minute when Besancon's Gilles Contat scored an own goal from a corner taken by Brazilian Rai.

But they had to wait until the 69th minute to secure the match when striker Cyrille Pouget, newly signed from Servette of Switzerland, scored his first goal for the Parisian club. France international Patrice Loko, a late substitute for Pouget, added the third eight minutes from time.

PORTUGAL - Benfica captain Joao Pinto was sent off in his club's 1-0 defeat away to Guimaraes on Sunday as Porto extended their commanding lead in the Portuguese first division with a crushing 5-0 win over Braga.

Porto, who appear unassailable in their bid for a third successive championship, top the table with 44 points, 11 ahead of Benfica. Sporting, who drew 2-2 against Belenenses on Friday, are in third place with 31 points.
Guimaraes captain Quim Berto scored a penalty after he was fouled in the eighth minute by Benfica's Belgian goalkeeper Michel Preud'homme.
Porto routed Braga at home as league top scorer Mario Jardel of Brazil scored two of his side's five goals. Zlatko Zahovic, Edmilson Pimenta and substitute Antonio Folha scored Porto's other goals.
